correctness.rationale: For a>=b>0, the positive-quadrant section g(t)=sqrt(sqrt(1+t^4)-sqrt(a^4+b^4*t^4)) has g*g'' exactly the stated algebraic combination of S,R. With u=a²,v=b²,q=R/S, convexity reduces to 3(q³−u²v²)(1−q)>=(u²−q²)(q²−v²). The condition b>=a² gives u²<=v<=q<=u<1; lower-bounding the left by 3q²(1−q)(q−v) and upper-bounding the right by 2q²(1−q)(q−v) proves convexity. The perspective of g is convex and the defect is coordinatewise increasing, yielding complex triangle inequality. Conversely, absolute norms have coordinatewise monotonicity; if 0<b<a² then the coefficient of t⁴ near the b-axis in defect(t,1)² is (1−a⁴/b²)/2<0, and if b=0<a the t² term is negative. The a=b and a=b=0 boundary cases work. I independently checked the exact second derivative by SymPy and many rational inequalities and explicit outside-threshold failures; the proof is analytic for all parameters.
